candidates.why: Must Read: rare controlled negative result — 3 evolution frameworks x 10 backbones x 4 verified environments, with a hand-verified-experience control cleanly separating 'wrong lessons' from 'right lessons that still don't transfer'.
candidates.caveat: Held-out evaluation uses a single rollout per checkpoint on small sets (WebArena Reddit = 27 tasks) with no confidence intervals, so headline declines (25.93%->7.41%) are directionally alarming but noisy.

candidates.why: Not a Must Read: pure computability theory (authors concede Theorem 1 is close to a restatement of Rice's theorem) with zero experiments — formalization is not validation, and no bridge to bounded-capability proposers is measured.
candidates.caveat: No experiments, simulations, or case studies; the connection to real pipelines (reward models, AI-Scientist reviewers) is made by interpretation, not measurement.

candidates.why: Strong existence proof with excellent measurement hygiene (sealed held-out twins, multi-seed, paired CIs), but one campaign on one 4B base, parity only 'statistically indistinguishable', and the mean is carried by ALFWorld — edged out by better-replicated evidence elsewhere.
candidates.caveat: No human-recipe control at matched budget, and the four 'replicates' share data, notes, and checkpoints, so they are not independent.

candidates.why: Must Read: real 64-128 GPU campaigns with equal-budget comparisons (OptiCo/BO/random), an agent-independent correctness gate with measured 0/133 false-reject and 16/24 fault-catch rates, and an honest +0.0% no-op on Mixtral.
candidates.caveat: Only the models were held out — stack, accelerators, and agent model are those used in development; n=3 campaigns yields p=0.05-0.125, and the +33.9% partly measures porting friction of H100 recipes onto B200.

candidates.why: Not a Must Read: single-seed, 5,000-step, loss-only evidence — the 1.18e-2 validation-loss margin over AGC (~0.6% relative) could plausibly be within seed-to-seed noise; internal stack, no code release.
candidates.caveat: Every condition is one run with seed 48; the margins over AGC and SSC-constant are small relative to plausible run-to-run variance, and no error bars or repeats are reported.

candidates.why: Exemplary statistics (7 paired seeds, sign-flip tests) and a proven impossibility theorem, but every practical gain requires a deliberately imposed imbalance edit — at lambda=0 SAGGS is neutral-to-negative, so it is evidence for checkpoint-surgery recovery, not ordinary training.
candidates.caveat: No demonstrated benefit for ordinary training without an imposed edit; natural pair drift in the authors' own runs (Q-K log-ratio ~0.15) appears too small to matter.

candidates.why: Must Read: a provable failure mode of symmetric reward aggregation (Theorem 1) empirically confirmed across 5 models, 2 families, 2 domains, and compatible/incompatible rewards, with a structural fix (TAG) that is the only arm surviving the no-op reward setting.
candidates.caveat: All auxiliary channels are synthetic and binary (no learned reward models or rubric judges tested), and headline 'every method collapses' rests partly on simplified ports (the Lagrangian dual decays to correctness-only within ~20 steps).

candidates.why: The week's best evaluation hygiene (held-out judges/corpora, blind human annotation at p=0.01, component ablations, anti-gaming checks), but the copy test is purely lexical and baselines were trained once — the area's second slot yielded to cross-area coverage.
candidates.caveat: A close paraphrase counts as 'authored', so ASC does not structurally detect semantic copying, and everything downstream inherits the reward checker's blind spots at <=9B scale.

candidates.why: Pre-registered, confound-controlled testbed with causal rent decomposition and a proper audit experiment, but everything runs at 1-2B parameters with 'gold' itself operationalized by learned reward models, and audits only in one grid cell.
candidates.caveat: Policies and proxy RMs are 1-2B parameters with English-only prompts; the bunching threshold-evasion interval covers zero, and the audit study is Qwen x Qwen only.

candidates.why: Not a Must Read: all results are NeuroSim behavioral simulation with no silicon or array-level measurement, on small workloads, and the +87-point headline is against a catastrophically failing representation (1.4% accuracy).
candidates.caveat: Simulation-only validation; the cost proxy is a conservative estimate rather than a placed-and-routed design, and no comparison against noise-aware training baselines is quantified.

candidates.why: A serious 3,200 GPU-hour campaign opening a real axis, but the central taxonomy-labeling procedure is never specified and results appear only as stacked-distribution figures without numeric tables or confidence intervals.
candidates.caveat: How corrupted outputs were assigned to Categories I-IV (manual vs automated, agreement) is absent — the single biggest reproducibility gap, since the entire distribution analysis depends on it.

candidates.why: Must Read: externally validated testing research — 39 upstream reports, 35 developer-confirmed, 18 already fixed; 99.26% oracle precision on 50,074 labeled cases; the retain-vs-reset replay protocol cleanly isolates compiler-state corruption.
candidates.caveat: The dramatic coverage gains are on the paper's own behavior-coverage metrics (compiler source-line coverage moves only 14.17%->14.94%), and 22 of 35 stateful bugs are in PyTorch alone.

candidates.why: Must Read: turns 'when can an agent trust compiled memory' into exact change-detection theory, then validates on replayed identical streams — 0 false certifications in 5,779 at-risk epochs and 7-73x fewer stale answers than ExpeL/ACE-style counters.
candidates.caveat: Requires exact verifiers (KB execution, unit tests); the headline benchmark is bespoke with nearly-total staleness that flatters detectors, and the ExpeL/ACE baselines are idealized vote-per-audit transplants.

candidates.why: 17,428 human judgments and 38 real triggered exploits with 1-366-line fixes are strong, but the normative 'expected contract' is self-derived (GPT-5.6 agents reviewed by the paper's own authors) and only 7% of gaps sit on a threat chain — an order of magnitude below the headline.
candidates.caveat: The agreement statistics (AC1 0.95) measure reviewer consistency, not ground truth, so the 63% gap rate remains partially a function of how strict the derivation agent's admission criteria are.

candidates.why: Clean paired-probe design with an exceptional robustness battery, but the single-family primary pipeline (anonymized HY4-preview) both generates and answers the probes — a structural bias toward execution-resident detail.
candidates.caveat: The DeepSeek replication validates the sign and rough magnitude of the gap, not the identical probe set, and the 37-task cohort is non-random, Python-only, and underrepresents harder issues.

candidates.why: Must Read: decisive, Lean-formalized refutation of QEP's published universal guarantee (a two-scalar first-order counterexample) plus pre-registered 8B experiments showing fixed alpha=1/2 always beats RTN while selection-based strength rules overfit — the area's most rigorous evidence.
candidates.caveat: The positive guarantee covers linear networks under subtractive dither on an unbounded grid — an idealized scheme no deployed system uses — and all theorems fix the calibration input, saying nothing about held-out degradation.

candidates.why: Genuinely clean multi-angle causal diagnosis (termination signal survives, preference shifts toward repetition) with permutation tests, but gains are modest (+1.3-3.7 points), the default pipeline is the authors' own OBC-Prune, and AIME cells are noise-dominated.
candidates.caveat: The cross-pipeline claim rests on 8 settings from a single model family, and at high sparsity capability is genuinely destroyed — only weight updates (Masked-LoRA) recover it.

candidates.why: Well-ablated scaling law validated on an external grid, but everything is validated only up to 910M non-embedding parameters — the compute-optimal predictions at 10^20+ FLOPs extrapolate the functional form 2-3 orders of magnitude beyond fitted data.
candidates.caveat: The training corpus is never named, no code or run data is released, and the cost model ignores all non-GEMM operations with speedups fixed from a single kernel measurement.

candidates.why: Must Read: converts CAA fragility into measurable curvature geometry with systematic controls (36/36 token-level reversals, 25/25 generation wins over CAA, PCA/random/sign-flip/k-sweep checks) and a one-line fix — including the safety finding that CAA degrades Qwen refusal 78%->36%.
candidates.caveat: Compared only against vanilla (and sign-flipped) CAA — no head-to-head with conceptors, SAE-guided, or optimization-based steering — and generation evidence is 50 greedy completions per condition.

candidates.why: Extraordinarily disciplined causal pipeline (frozen protocols, pre-written rules falsified and honored, human-validated labels), but the testbed is a toy (one-line tasks, three-item workspaces) and all 'five for five' claims live inside a 5-of-13 model-family eligibility filter.
candidates.caveat: The headline IRR metric rests on a simulated budgeted-overseer whose seed-1 estimate ranges 0.45-0.95 across overseer seeds, and the one stable localized-editing win is a single family.

candidates.why: Genuinely causal stage-by-stage circuit tracing with pre-registered rules and Bonferroni-corrected statistics, but scope is English multiple-choice only and the circuit itself plays 'only a modest role' in free-form sycophancy.
candidates.caveat: The 70B RL null is uninformative (the released update changes weights 45x less than 8B), so the RL-strengthens-cues claim really rests on 7B-13B, and the swap evidence covers only suggested-answer cues.

candidates.why: Honest production postmortem with out-of-sample cost-model validation and six upstream PRs, but every condition was run exactly once, latency covers a single 14.7k-17.9k token bucket, and the 124x headline is against its own pathological configuration.
candidates.caveat: Against recompute on the same requests the best config wins p99 by only ~1.9x and its median hit (0.40 s) is still 0.09 s slower than recomputing; the 98.5% hit rate was engineered to fit the private instance.

candidates.why: Proofs, released code, 50-iteration error bars, and a convergence check are commendable, but on FA3-supported masks it runs at 0.71-1.00x of vanilla FlashAttention-3 — it buys expressiveness, not speed, and the end-to-end gain is 7.3-11% over its own ablated baseline.
candidates.caveat: The end-to-end comparison baseline is the same system with new components disabled (not Megatron or MagiAttention end-to-end), and the stack is Hopper + NVSHMEM + PaddlePaddle specific.

candidates.why: Must Read: the area's strongest measured systems evidence — a real 128-GPU H20 cluster, three tuned baselines on the same veRL substrate, 3 repeats with std, per-component ablations, and equal RL convergence in ~30 h vs >50 h wall-clock.
candidates.caveat: All results use a single math dataset with a hybrid verifiable+generative reward (the GenRM setting tested in its least GenRM-dependent form), the throughput objective counts only rollout+reward tokens, and no code is released.

candidates.why: Reference-grade process transparency (fractional-factorial ANOVA mixtures, license-clean data reproduction, released configs) but the model itself is mid-tier — on par in Japanese, clearly behind in English and reasoning — so the evidence supports a governance template, not a research finding.
candidates.caveat: The 32.14B-total MoE is compared against 8B/20B models with no total-parameter-matched or FLOP-matched baseline, and gpt-oss-synthesized training data judged by a same-family judge is an unexamined bias.

candidates.why: Useful open artifact, but the 'SOTA' framing is selective (loses OSWorld-Verified by 9.7 and TerminalBench 2.1 by 9.0 to Qwen3.6-27B) and the headline on-device use case is never quantified — no latency or throughput numbers appear anywhere.
candidates.caveat: Only two competitors are compared, several baseline numbers are self-reported, and claims like 'on-policy distillation consistently improves downstream RL' are given without numbers.

candidates.why: Not a Must Read: a self-evaluated technical report whose baselines are transplanted from prior papers rather than re-run, with a single primary checkpoint, no seeds or error bars, and understanding wins concentrated in document/chart niches while trailing on MMMU, MathVista, and RealWorldQA.
candidates.caveat: Cross-paper comparability (decoding settings, prompts, judges) is asserted rather than controlled, and the NVIDIA reference run underperforms the Ascend run by wide margins (e.g., 3D MM-Vet 43.8 vs 50.5).
